title: 🤖 Forward Mobile can deadlock shader and pipeline compilation with one worker
body:
> [!INFO] *AI disclosure*: This contribution was authored by on an autonomous AI agent, on behalf of a user to report a Godot rendering deadlock identified through application testing.

### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: Godot 4.7.1.stable.official [a13da4feb], official Android x86_64 debug export template.
- Runtime reproduction has not yet been repeated with 4.7.2. However, the relevant Forward Mobile lock scopes are unchanged in 4.7.2-stable and current `master` [20a52a8988b1], so the demonstrated lock cycle is still present in source.

### System information

Android 10 (API 29) x86_64 emulator, 1 vCPU, 2048 MiB RAM - Godot v4.7.1.stable.official [a13da4feb] - Vulkan 1.3.0 (Forward Mobile) - llvmpipe (LLVM 21.0.0, 256 bits)

### Issue description

Forward Mobile can deadlock while shader variants and graphics pipelines are being compiled concurrently. The hang was observed while loading a 3D scene containing imported skinned meshes with multiple `StandardMaterial3D` shader variants. It is timing-sensitive with larger worker pools, but becomes repeatable when Godot has one worker thread.

Native thread dumps captured after 10, 30, and 90 seconds were identical. Disassembling the exact official Android template and resolving the program counters shows this cycle:

```text
Main/VkThread
  SceneShaderForwardMobile::ShaderData::is_valid()
    locks SceneShaderForwardMobile::singleton_mutex
  ShaderRD::version_is_valid()
  ShaderRD::_compile_ensure_finished()
  ShaderRD::_compile_version_end()
  WorkerThreadPool::wait_for_group_task_completion()
    waits for a ShaderCompilation group task

WorkerThread 0 (the only worker)
  PipelineCompilation task
  SceneShaderForwardMobile::ShaderData::_create_pipeline()
  SceneShaderForwardMobile::ShaderData::get_shader_variant()
    waits for SceneShaderForwardMobile::singleton_mutex
```

The main/render thread owns `SceneShaderForwardMobile::singleton_mutex` while waiting for a worker-pool group task. The only worker is itself waiting for that same mutex, so the queued shader-compilation task cannot run. This is an engine lock-order/scheduling deadlock; Vulkan is not being called by either blocked thread at the top of the captured stacks.

The relevant calls are visible in the current source:

- [`get_shader_variant()` and `is_valid()` both acquire `singleton_mutex`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/forward_mobile/scene_shader_forward_mobile.cpp#L481-L512).
- [`ShaderRD::_compile_version_end()` waits for the worker-pool group`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shader_rd.cpp#L737-L743).

This appears to be the Forward Mobile counterpart of #102877. Commit 09282c316a77c0e5beda9610e6a87f133ace5e94 fixed that issue by reducing mutex scope in Forward Clustered, including removing the outer singleton lock from `get_shader_variant()`, `is_valid()`, native-source access, and destruction. Forward Mobile was not changed. The omission was also [called out during the original issue discussion](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/102877#issuecomment-2695456644).

Expected behavior: loading a scene must finish regardless of worker-pool size and shader/pipeline scheduling order. A slow software Vulkan implementation may make compilation slow, but it should not produce an indefinite wait cycle.

Suggested fix: port the applicable Forward Clustered lock-scope changes from commit 09282c316a77c0e5beda9610e6a87f133ace5e94 to `forward_mobile/scene_shader_forward_mobile.cpp`:

1. Limit the `set_code()` singleton lock to `compiler.compile()` rather than holding it across ShaderRD version operations.
2. Remove the redundant outer singleton lock around thread-safe ShaderRD version calls in `get_native_source_code()`, `get_native_shader_and_version()`, `get_shader_variant()`, `is_valid()`, and the `ShaderData` destructor.
3. Keep `MaterialData::update_parameters()` from querying a ShaderRD version while holding the singleton lock. Current `master` already retrieves its shader RID before taking that lock.

`ShaderRD` protects version operations with per-version mutexes, so this would align Forward Mobile with the established Forward Clustered fix rather than introducing a new synchronization design.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an Android project using the Mobile Vulkan renderer.
2. Add a 3D scene containing at least two imported skinned mesh instances whose `StandardMaterial3D` resources compile different shader variants (for example, one material using a normal map and one without). A cold shader/pipeline cache makes the scheduling window easier to hit.
3. Export with the official Godot 4.7.1 Android x86_64 debug template.
4. Run it on an x86_64 Android emulator configured with one virtual CPU and a Vulkan software renderer.
5. Load or instantiate the scene immediately after startup.

The process can stop making progress indefinitely during scene construction. Repeated native thread dumps show the stable cycle above. Removing the distinct normal-mapped material variant, or increasing available worker threads, avoids the observed scheduling order but does not fix the lock-order defect.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

A redistributable standalone MRP has not yet been isolated. The trigger is timing-sensitive and the smallest procedural mesh/material probes tried so far did not reliably schedule pipeline and shader compilation in the conflicting order. The native stacks above identify the cycle directly, and a single-worker Android emulator makes it repeatable with a scene containing multiple imported skinned-mesh material variants.
